title: The round-5 FIND-103 fix (buildSubmittedPatch now PRESERVES the original bank notes via info.raw) RE-OPENS a double-pay path: a 'submitted'/'needs_review' row that an operator re-queues is now fully re-parseable by parseBankRecipient and will be DISPATCHED TO GMO A SECOND TIME. There is no guard rejecting a row that already carries 'submitted'/'ref='.
description:
Trace the round-5 edit end to end. After a successful submit, markPaid (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:189-193) calls buildSubmittedPatch(info), which now writes notes = `${info.raw};submitted;provider=...;amount=...;currency=...;ref=R1` (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:32-38). info.raw is the ORIGINAL bank notes threaded from claim->bankWatcherPass (rawById, bank-watcher.mjs:45,67) and originates from parseBankRecipient's `raw: row.notes` (lib/bank-recipients.mjs:24). So a 'submitted' row's notes now begin with the full `method=bank;country=jp;bankCode=0005;branchCode=001;accountType=...;accountNumber=...;beneficiaryName=...;claimed_at=...` string, followed by `;submitted;...;ref=R1`.

Now follow the DOCUMENTED operator-recovery path that is the entire justification for routing failures to needs_review instead of auto-requeue (FIND-100 design, restated in pollCompletions comment bank-payout-watcher.mjs:107-110: 'failed'->flagNeedsReview 'for a human/operator to confirm with GMO before any re-send'). pollCompletions failed->flagNeedsReview sets status='needs_review' WITHOUT changing notes (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:117,166), so the needs_review row still carries the full bank fields + `;ref=R1`. When the operator performs the recovery action the design names ('manually re-queues'), i.e. flips status back to 'queued', the next pass does:
  readBankRecipients (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:125-129) reads status=eq.queued -> picks up the row.
  parseBankRecipient (lib/bank-recipients.mjs:15-34): parseNotes builds a kv map; the FIRST segment is still `method=bank`, country=jp, and every bank field is present (the trailing `submitted` token has no '=' so parseNotes ignores it; provider/amount/currency/ref/claimed_at are extra kv that parseBankRecipient never inspects). kv.method==='bank' and all four required bank fields are present -> RETURNS A VALID RECIPIENT.
  bankWatcherPass claims, plans, and DISPATCHES it to makeGmoAdapter -> submitBulkTransfer again. The money for ref=R1 is sent A SECOND TIME.

There is NO guard anywhere that rejects a row already carrying a ref/submitted marker: grep of bank-watcher.mjs and lib/bank-recipients.mjs for ref=/submitted/already/hasRef finds only comments, no logic. parseBankRecipient does not look at parseRef(notes); bankWatcherPass does not check for an existing ref before dispatch.

This is a STRICT REGRESSION from round-5's pre-fix state. The round-5 FIND-103 part-(2) write-up itself states the PRE-fix behavior was money-SAFE: an operator re-queue of a post-submit row 'parses to null and is dropped... never re-paid' — a no-op that merely defeated recovery intent (low severity). The round-5 fix made that row parseable, which is exactly what converts the money-SAFE no-op into a money-UNSAFE re-dispatch. The fix optimized the WRONG variable: it restored parseability without adding the de-dupe guard that parseability now requires. The FIND-103 recommendation ('keep the original bank notes... so a re-queued row remains parseable') was followed literally, but its second half ('add a test for a re-queued post-submit row') was implemented only as a happy-path assertion that the row parses (bank-payout-watcher.test.js:72-80 asserts back.bank.bankCode==='0005') — the test CELEBRATES the re-parseability that is the bug, and asserts nothing about NOT re-dispatching a row that carries ref=R1.
recommendation: Add a hard de-dupe guard at the dispatch boundary so a row that has already been submitted can NEVER be re-paid, even if its status is flipped back to 'queued': in parseBankRecipient (or in readBankRecipients/bankWatcherPass before claim) reject/skip any row whose notes contain parseRef(notes)!==null OR a 'submitted' token, routing it to needs_review instead of the fanout. Alternatively, the operator-recovery contract must be a DISTINCT clean re-queue that writes FRESH notes with no ref (and the code must still refuse to dispatch any notes carrying ref=). Add a test: a row with notes `method=bank;...;ref=R1` set to status=queued must NOT appear in bankRecipientsFromRows / must NOT be dispatched. Until such a guard exists, this is a live double-pay lever reachable through the very operator path the design relies on.
